title: Latency fallthrough handoff — routing/auth/quotas weeknote 2027-12-15
content:
Attendees: Priya (note), Diego, Ava, Liam, Sofia, oncall: mkhan

Purpose: quick weekly handoff focused on recent latency spikes that surfaced when route-fallthrough logic triggered during regional capacity pressure. Capture action items for routing, auth, and quota owners and sketch a short experiment plan to reduce tail latency.

Summary of last 48h:
- 2027-12-14 03:12 UTC: two brief bursts of 95th/99th percentile latency across eu-west-1 for control-plane route decisions. Correlated with a surge of low-priority requests and quota lookups hitting the auth cache miss path.
- Failure mode: fallback routing kicked in to fallback-tier model variant; fallback introduced extra KV-cache warmup and additional auth checks (token revalidation). Combined added ~80–150ms per request at p99.
- Traffic picture: ~15% increase in global synthetic traffic (scheduled load test) + organic customer traffic; peak qps 3.6k, normal baseline for the window ~3.0k.
- Mitigations applied: increased auth cache TTL for service tokens (temp), raised quota local-cache size on the route decision plane, explicit prioritized batching for warmup sequences.

Metrics snapshot (pre/post mitigation):
- p50/p95/p99 (control-plane decision time) before: 8ms / 42ms / 220ms; after: 9ms / 36ms / 120ms (partial improvement).
- Auth cache miss rate spiked from 0.8% -> 7.4% during burst.
- Route fallback rate peaked at 4.1% (normal <0.4%).

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
1) Synthetic load + organic burst produced an unusual distribution of sequence lengths; many requests came with extended prompt prefixes which invalidated some per-customer KV cache locality assumptions.
2) Route fallback logic currently serializes a small set of extra checks (auth revalidate and quota double-check) synchronously; when fallback happens frequently, the extra round-trips amplify tail latency.
3) Our local quota cache eviction policy is size-based only; during concurrency spikes we observed cache churn leading to extra RPCs to quota service.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How often do customers submit the specific prefix pattern that defeats KV locality? (Data team to run histogram analysis on prompt lengths and prefix fingerprints)
- Can fallback route decision be made more speculative (return warm candidate and inline async re-eval) without violating SLAs?
- Does auth token refresh logic have an internal backoff we can tune per-tier?

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Diego: implement a quick speculative-fallback prototype (non-blocking auth revalidate). PR branch: platform/speculative-fallback; target: 2027-12-22 for prod experiment.
- Ava: add a short-lived increased TTL override for service tokens for eu-west-1 for 48 hours and monitor auth miss rate; done in emergency window, follow-up adjust to 60s safe value; ETA: 2027-12-16.
- Liam: change quota local-cache eviction from pure-LRU to hotspot-aware policy (promote accesses by request-affinity); spike test in staging by 2027-12-20.
- Sofia: run telemetry job to produce prefix-fingerprint histograms and cross-correlation with KV cache misses (JIRA PLT-4380); results by 2027-12-18.
- Priya: write a concise runbook stub for oncall when route-fallback crosses 1% sustained for >5m; add to Confluence and link in the incident dashboard; ETA: 2027-12-17.

Experiment plan (fast turnaround):
- Objective: reduce p99 decision-time during fallback events by 40% without increasing incorrect route selection.
- Hypotheses: (A) speculative auth revalidate reduces critical-path time; (B) hotspot-aware cache reduces miss amplification.
- Staging test: replay the 12-14 burst trace in canary namespace with feature flags: speculative-fallback=on, quota-hotspot-cache=on; measure p50/p95/p99 and route correctness over 2h window.
- Rollout plan: canary -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% within 72h if no regression on cost or correctness.

Rollback & safety:
- If route correctness drops (detected by routing-eval alert), roll back speculative-fallback immediate and pause quota eviction change.
- Observability: add per-request metadata tag when speculative path used to trace mismatches.

Notes to self / meeting fragments (informal):
- rough idea: could we keep a tiny ephemeral per-node prefix cache (approx 128 keys) that stores last-seen prompt tokens fingerprint -> route decision? Might hit locality without global state. Pros: faster on local hits; Cons: memory + staleness.
- question for infra: do we have headroom on control-plane pods to allocate 2–4MB extra per pod for tiny prefix cache? (cc: infra perf team)

Blockers:
- spec fallback requires changes spanning routing, auth API, and the SDK header shape (need coordination with SDK team to set a short 'speculative' header). Until SDK header change is accepted, the prototype will be limited to internal clients. (Ticket: PLT-4420)
- quota-hotspot cache needs a small schema tweak in telemetry emitted by quota service to expose 'access affinity' metric.

Next meeting (handoff cadence):
- Short follow-up on 2027-12-17 09:00 UTC: quick sync to validate Sofia's telemetry output.
- Full feature sync (spec/prod rollout) 2027-12-21 16:00 UTC.

Decision log (so far):
- Temporary mitigation: increase auth token TTL in eu-west-1 (Ava) approved.
- Longer-term: prioritize speculative-fallback prototype and quota cache improvement in next sprint cycle.

Attachments / quick links:
- Incident trace (internal): link-proxy/trace/2027-12-14-fallthrough-01
- Staging repro script: gitlab:/ops/replays/fallthrough-burst-2027

Freeform / brainstorm bullets (raw):
- Could we add a 'warmup' flag on route-fallback that triggers a lightweight prefetch of the KV keys most likely to be needed? (warmup TTL 250ms)
- Consider adding a lightweight heuristic: if request QPS < 20% and route-stability > 60s, prefer local-fallback path (less strict auth check). Safety review required.
- Testing note: replay scripts must preserve exact arrival jitter to reproduce tail behavior.

If you see other signals in your dashboards (particularly quota eviction counter or auth replay errors) paste them here — I'll compile and push update before the Friday handoff.

-- Priya
